plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since I win only if my bid is highest, and I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $22. Bidding my true value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay.

This is a second-price auction, where the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value. Bidding your value ensures you win whenever your value exceeds both opponents' bids (maximizing profit), and you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher risks paying more than your value if others bid between your value and your bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Thus, the optimal bid equals my value of $34.

This is a second-price auction, so the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and I never pay more than my value if I win. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if others bid between my value and my inflated bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $10, I'll bid $10 to maximize expected profit.
